title: September 2026 reseller acquisition spending and support decision
content:
September 2026 spending and support decision

Mara Ellison, September 1, 2026. Evidence cutoff: August 31. Under POL-AUTH-3 I approve Option B, effective upon implementation today: retain CAM-DECOR and AS-DECOR active at $65 daily. Pause CAM-START and AS-START, and CAM-RETURN and AS-RETURN, setting each parent and ad-set daily budget to $0. Pause the corresponding START and RETURN ads. Preserve decorator creative/delivery, history, completed campaigns and the unlaunched fall draft.

Evidence and judgment

I considered Imani Brooks's delivered mail-acq-fit-f293bf34cc894351a699d9f2c8ef4659, Owen Delgado's mail-acq-orders-f1137d63fdc140ed9b62c8ebf83410c8 and SH-ACQ-ORDER-CHECK, and Priya Nair's mail-priya-acq-comparison-9af43079877d4ad4847d42ce441d8321 with SH-ACQ-COMPARISON and SH-ACQ-OPTIONS. Their reports incorporate SH-SOURCES, recorded campaign spending and the commercial ledger. Source permissions remain unchanged.

Imani distinguishes nine intake records from eight identities. Seven are first applications, but Hillcrest is an own-use school buyer, so seven is not a count of eligible resellers. Alder is already a customer and Moonrise's August visitor inquiry repeats its July application. The July–August subset contains eight records and seven identities; adding Riverbend's May application produces nine and eight.

DECOR has concrete commercial needs: Riverbend's visitor-center tees and totes, Kestrel's screen-printed restaurant tees, and Oakline's embroidery/heat-transfer business adding resale. Riverbend documents were accepted May 19. Kestrel still needs a signed certificate and actual color/size quantities; its estimated 240 tees and $1,008 opportunity are not an accepted order. Oakline awaits central certificate review. START includes Moonrise's missing sales tax license, Dovetail's unclear buyers, channels and decoration arrangements, and Hillcrest's end-user request. RETURN combines Slate Run's legal-name issue, existing Alder resource demand and the repeated Moonrise contact.

Owen establishes Riverbend's 600 × $4.20 = $2,520 invoiced purchase, with no matching posted credit through August 31, as the only observed invoiced value among reviewed new relationships. Removing Riverbend leaves zero. Six unresolved applicants have no invoices in the supplied Drive ledger. Alder's $604.80 July purchase predates its August inquiry. Summit's older $2,820 less $141 posted credit = $2,679 is separate from its $3,456 accepted unallocated order. Northfork's $630 accepted commitment remains subject to allocation and cancellation consent; closing the duplicate ticket does not resolve the live exception. Mesa's $633.60 invoice remains unpaid and its $79.20 claim is unposted. Orchard's $1,132.80 less $141.60 credit = $991.20 and A002's $1,728 less $96 = $1,632 are historical context, not current-campaign acquisition. Unallocated commitments and unposted claims are not realized net purchases. Sheets Orders and the Drive ledger have different coverage and must not be added together.

Priya's common July–August comparison gives DECOR $3,800/102 results = $37.25 per platform result; START $2,900/163 = $17.79; RETURN $1,550/75 = $20.67. Checked totals are $8,250 and 340 platform results. May–August operating histories are respectively $6,600/178, $3,900/225 and $1,550/75; starts occurred in May, June and July. The common period aligns delivery dates, not applicant maturity: Riverbend applied in May and purchased in July.

The matched intake set is incomplete and is not a complete funnel. Platform results are not distinct qualified businesses. Account matching does not prove advertising caused a purchase. Audience differences, timing, uncertain source links and concentrated observations prevent confident conversion forecasts, causal return, profit or advertising ROI claims. A low platform result cost cannot establish an economically useful qualified acquisition.

Two practical choices and checked costs

Option A maintains all three campaigns at $65/$45/$25 daily. September planning exposure is (65+45+25) × 30 = $4,050. Estimated additional weekly representative/services/marketing hours are 12/6/8, costing 12×48 + 6×42 + 8×50 = $1,228. It includes decorator commercial development, additional starter discovery/document guidance and visitor triage. This buys broader learning but spends more effort on unclear readiness and repeated relationships.

Option B retains decorator media alone: $65 × 30 = $1,950 planning exposure. Additional weekly hours are 6/3/4, costing 6×48 + 3×42 + 4×50 = $288+$126+$200 = $614. Compared with A, B saves $2,100 planned media and $614 estimated internal support each week. Using an explicit 30/7 convention, September-equivalent internal support estimates are $5,262.86 for A and $2,631.43 for B; these are estimates, not wages paid or vendor invoices. Both options add $0 production purchases and fit the $6,000 monthly media authority. Existing production obligations remain under the separate $1,200 authority.

I select B because the clearer decorator business needs justify bounded continuation. I accept the higher decorator cost per platform result for specific useful commercial work, but challenge expansion because the observed invoiced outcome rests entirely on Riverbend. Cheap starter results and mixed returning-visitor identities do not yet justify their extra proactive acquisition support. Pausing them sacrifices learning breadth and may miss good unlinked prospects; this is a reversible allocation, not a rejection of existing applicants or customers.

Protected capacity and named work

Protect weekly application/services/catalog blocks of 10/12/8 hours. The 18/14/16 discretionary allowances are additional and already follow recurring commitments: do not subtract recurring obligations twice. A leaves 6/8/8 discretionary hours; B leaves 12/11/12. Preserve the September 3 Orchard City uniform review, Priya's September 3 catalog work, open service exceptions, Spanish sleeve wording and the corrected translation invoice.

B's additional representative envelope comprises 3 hours conditional Kestrel commercial preparation, 1 Oakline discovery, 1 Riverbend development and 1 Alder resource clarification. Services has 1 hour readiness/document handoffs and 2 commercial/order checks. Marketing has 2 hours approved-resource reuse and 2 linkage/pacing checks. Routine application requests stay in the protected application block. These are planning envelopes, not completed calls; unavailable prerequisites do not justify invented work. Owen must now use Priya's actual comparison and this allocation to substantively check the 3-hour services plan against accepted commitments, distinguishing protected exceptions from additional acquisition work. If actual effort threatens protected work, reduce acquisition activity and escalate the tradeoff to me.

Imani owns seven customer follow-up tasks with associated notes: by September 2 at 16:00 Pacific, obtain Kestrel's signed certificate and actual color/size split, follow up Oakline's central review, request Moonrise's license in its existing application thread, and offer Hillcrest an appropriate reseller resource. By September 3 at 16:00 Pacific, clarify Dovetail's business, selling channels, decoration arrangements and required documents; route Slate Run's legal-name explanation for central reconciliation; and clarify Alder's resource needs. A single Moonrise task covers both intakes. Preserve all six unresolved applications as open. Gareth retains documentary acceptance and credit authority; Lucia retains order and amendment decisions. No fulfillment, acceptance, payment or customer response is presumed.

Controls and reconsideration

Priya must implement and verify exact parent/ad-set/ad controls, then report them to all three colleagues. With CBO false, ad-set budgets are effective; parent amounts mirror them and must not be counted again. $65 daily for 30 days is planning exposure, not a native hard monthly cap. Priya owns business-day checks of delivered and accrued September spend and must reduce or pause before exceeding the $1,950 allocation, seeking a recorded amendment before an increase. The $4,050 unused media authority is not authorization to spend. The account's $36,000 spendCap is not a September cap. Preserve August expense and the $650 unpaid balance; this decision makes no payment.

Review September 15 and again September 30. START remains paused pending clearer eligible business/channel/decoration evidence, progress on missing documents through central review, and reporting separating new eligible relationships from end users and repeat contacts. RETURN remains paused pending a central response on Slate Run's legal name and reporting that separates new applicants, existing-customer resource demand and repeated applicants. Any restart requires a useful incremental support scope and stronger distinct-customer evidence, with recorded approval. Customers may resume useful individual support when prerequisites arrive without an automatic advertising restart. Hillcrest receives a reseller resource; wholesale support would require evidence of a different eligible reseller purpose.

DECOR continuation is conditional too: check Kestrel and Oakline progress, distinct-business quality beyond Riverbend, actual support hours and spending pace. Reduce or pause if fit weakens, papers stagnate or existing obligations are threatened. No future revenue or acceptance is promised. Final implementation acceptance remains pending Priya's verified controls, Imani's task/note records and Owen's substantive post-allocation feasibility report.
